title.narrative: Community Action for Peace and Socio-Economic Development

description.narrative: One year into the implementation of the Community Action for Peace and Socio-economic Development (CAPSED) in Goska, Dangoma, Kurmin Masara, Zangon Urban and Zangon Kataf communities has enriched WIC’s knowledge of the staggering poverty and environmental degradation due to insecurity and the absence of peace. The community poverty induced by insecurity has transformed farmers into charcoal merchants. This soaring business has resulted from a transformation of forest areas into plains. This has added pressure on the already degraded land and reduced its capacity to sustain present and future generations. If this trend is unchecked, it might compel farmers to join herders in the southwards migration challenge with its attendant impact conflict. Besides the economic costs of insecurity and the staggering poverty it has caused across the country, it is gradually destroying the trust between and within cultures and religions. Consequently, families are being destroyed and so are communities and our nascent democracy is also in danger.
